s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic cutaneous lesions with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Asymptomatic cutaneous lesions on the face, trunk, and extremities
Monomorphic keratotic papules and symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques
key_facts: Lesions progressively spread to the trunk and extremities
Multiple millimetric erythematous to hyperpigmented monomorphic keratotic papules
Symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques on the cheeks and temples
Mild anemia with hemoglobin level of 11.3 g/dL
Positive anti-Smith, SSA/Ro, SSB/La, and anti-U1RNP antibodies

shortlist.label: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-Smith, SSA/Ro, SSB/La, and anti-U1RNP antibodies, and characteristic skin lesions

shortlist.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Raised levels of antinuclear antibodies, hypocomplementemia, and moderate proteinuria

shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Characteristic skin lesions, including symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques on the cheeks and temples

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of lupus and rheumatoid arthritis features, including positive anti-U1RNP antibodies and mild arthralgias

shortlist.label: Rowell's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Coexistence of lupus erythematosus and erythema multiforme, with characteristic skin lesions and positive anti-nuclear antibodies

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of cutaneous lesions, including symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques on the cheeks and temples, along with the presence of anti-SSA/Ro and anti-SSB/La antibodies, is consistent with subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus. The absence of systemic features such as nephritis or seizures and the specific pattern of autoantibody positivity also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient has some systemic features such as mild anemia and proteinuria, the lack of more severe systemic involvement and the specific pattern of autoantibody positivity make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's lesions are more widespread and include the trunk and extremities, which is not typical of discoid lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: The patient's presentation does not meet the criteria for mixed connective tissue disease, which typically includes a combination of features from lupus, scleroderma, and rheumatoid arthritis.

rejected.label: Rowell's syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's presentation does not include the characteristic erythema multiforme-like lesions and the specific pattern of autoantibody positivity seen in Rowell's syndrome.
